Keep a Minecraft server running during that period.
Join and leave multiple times.
Perform a backup during the run.
Perform a scheduled operation.

Confirm server state remains accurate.
Confirm notifications do not become noisy/repetitive.
Confirm Player Activity remains sensible.

Do not explain Minecraft server administration.
Have them download Craft Conductor.
Have them launch it.
Have them create a modded server.
Have them start it.
Have them join from the same house.
Have them add a mod.
Have them send an invite to another person.
Have that person set up their Minecraft client without developer help.
Have that person connect from outside the home.
Restart the host PC.
Have the tester bring the server back online without developer help.
Perform a normal mod/update cycle.
Have the tester make a backup.
Have the tester restore it.
Trigger one understandable recoverable failure.
Confirm the tester understands what Craft Conductor says went wrong.
Confirm the tester can recover using the UI rather than Terminal/PowerShell.
Ask the tester: Would you feel comfortable running this for your kids without calling me?
Mark Dad Test PASS only if the answer is yes and the entire core journey completed without developer intervention.
Clean Windows install passes.
Real Fabric server passes.
Real modded server passes.

Real router/UPnP test passes on at least one router.
A non-UPnP/tunnel path passes.

Real backup/restore passes.

Full-disk behavior passes.

Update rehearsal result matches a real update.

Pick a mod that has no build for the chosen version and server type; confirm the row says Dependency unavailable, names which mod needs which, and offers Use Minecraft …, Choose another Minecraft version and Remove; confirm the version is not silently changed. (0.24.0)
Double-click Create my server (or press Enter twice); confirm one server and no red "port already used" message. (0.27.0)

Give the server a name in another language (Chinese, Korean, Hindi, Arabic, Vietnamese), with an emoji, and with accents ("Ángel's Café"); confirm it creates, reads the same after it has run, and Settings still saves. (0.27.0)

CurseForge as a modpack source: pick a CurseForge pack with Use this modpack; confirm its loader, Minecraft version, mods and configs come from the pack, and that pack mods the official server pack leaves out go to friends, not the server. (0.26.0)

Datapack build: for a mod with no build for your server type but a datapack on Modrinth, confirm Stay on Forge: use its datapack, the datapack is in the world's datapacks folder, and the map preview uses it. (0.26.0)
Change version on a mod: builds listed newest first, betas only when asked, mismatches marked; an update leaves a held mod alone until Newest. (0.26.0)

Add a Modrinth mod to the server that also runs on players' computers; confirm it, and its both-sides dependencies, were added to friends' mods with a message saying so. Remove it from the server; confirm it asks about friends' mods too. (0.27.0)
Drop a renamed CurseForge file into the manual-download box; confirm it is matched by checksum. (0.26.0)
Create a server from a pack that needs hand downloads; confirm Create my server waits, Load downloaded mods opens your Downloads folder, and Stop setting up works. (0.26.0)
Make a friends' mod problem; confirm invite links pause (friends opening an older link are told to try later) and Post to Discord and new links wait. (0.26.0)
Open an invite for a server with no `server-icon.png`; confirm the Craft Conductor icon shows, not a blank box. (0.26.0)
Confirm the pre-start mod check also runs in Check my setup, before an update, and for single-player (Install waits). (0.26.0)
This build runs Minecraft 26.x. Join and leave with a real client; confirm Connected Players, Online now and Player activity record them (26.x logs "System chat: … joined the game"). (0.27.0 fix)

Ban someone with a reason in Chinese or Russian, or with "Á", then ban/unban/op/whitelist while the server is stopped; confirm no ban disappears, and a damaged list is never replaced (a message says which file to fix). (0.27.0 fix)
Broadcast and console commands with "Café" and "大家好"; confirm the server and the Console show them intact. (0.27.0 fix)

On the Backups page, choose what backups hold; confirm secrets, IP bans and logs are off by default and that a backup says what it holds. Backups with secrets open only on this computer and account. (0.27.0)
Back up a running server with a large world; confirm the backup waits for the world-saved message (up to a minute) and warns in the activity if it never comes. (0.27.0)
Restore a Saved mod list (or go back with "Before …") that has a mod used as its datapack; confirm it stays a datapack. (0.27.0)
Update failure of Craft Conductor itself: confirm it says what went wrong and offers Try again, Retry connection, View update log and how to restart by hand. (0.25.0)
Confirm the previous version comes back if the new one does not come up in three minutes or stops right away, and the page says "The update to X didn't work, so Y is back." (0.25.0)
Confirm no new browser tab opens after an update; the open tab reloads itself. (0.25.0)
With two browsers open: the other one is told an update is under way and asked Launch the new version when it is ready, reloading only on acceptance. (0.25.0)

Later lasts until Craft Conductor is restarted, then is offered again; Check for Craft Conductor updates offers it at once; red dots on Craft Conductor settings, About & updates and Check for Craft Conductor updates while an update waits. (0.25.0)
Press Update now twice, or from two browsers; confirm one update starts. (0.25.0)
Phones with notifications on: told when an update is available, when Craft Conductor was updated, and when an update failed. (0.25.0)
Running servers come back after Craft Conductor updates itself, on the new version once it proves itself (or on the old one after a rollback); players see "Server restarting in 1 minute". (0.27.0)
Start, Restart, Stop: double-click each; confirm it counts once (no "busy: start is running"; Stop asks once). (0.27.0)
Keep making the map as I move is remembered after leaving the page and after reopening. (0.25.0)
Tick and untick Show Points of Interest; confirm hiding is immediate and, if they cannot be loaded, the map still works with Try again. (0.26.0)
Scroll the World-generation mods list and a new single-player game's mods; confirm they keep loading past 20. (0.26.0)
A backup (Every hour) and a restart (Every day at 4:00) due the same minute: confirm both happen, backup first. (0.27.0)

Keep Craft Conductor busy (a long update or backup) past a scheduled time by more than 10 minutes; confirm the backup or restart runs as soon as it is done, and a restart is not repeated if the server restarted meanwhile. (0.27.0)
Search the bug report also for the server's Discord webhook URL and CurseForge key, not only the password and tokens. (0.27.0)
A `[web] password` typed into `craft-conductor.toml` (or `hub.json`) becomes a hash the first time it is read; sign-in still works; backup notes do not keep it as typed. (0.27.0)

Files holding secrets (CurseForge key, Discord token and webhook, push and HTTPS keys, invite secrets, RCON password, a server's `craft-conductor.toml` or `server.properties` once it holds one, exports) are readable only by your account on Windows, including a folder on another drive. Check with `icacls`. (0.27.0)

Export server…: tick the world, mods and plugins, their settings, player lists, web map files, backups. Confirm passwords, keys and players' IP addresses go only when ticked, locked with a password shown once, and that Import a server... asks for it (or imports without them). (0.27.0)
Confirm an export no longer contains the Discord webhook URL or CurseForge key, and that after import Craft Conductor says to enter them again and where. (0.27.0)

Give a server the control panel's port, or the friends' download port, in Settings and on New server; confirm it is refused with a message saying which port is taken, and the reverse for the friends' download port. (0.27.0)
Occupy the control panel's port (8765) with another program; confirm Craft Conductor uses the next free port and opens it, and that a port set with `--web-port` is kept with a message. (0.27.0)
Quit Craft Conductor while Test these mods or Find which mods break it is booting a test server, or a map preview is generating; confirm no throwaway server keeps running afterwards. (0.27.0)

section: A. General / licensing (not tied to one section)

section: B. Firewall cleanup when a server is deleted
step: Delete a server that has a Craft Conductor firewall rule - The delete confirmation mentions the Windows Firewall rule. After deleting, an on-screen dialog offers Remove or Keep for the rule "Craft Conductor: <server> (TCP <port>)"; Remove shows Windows' administrator prompt and the rule is gone (`Get-NetFirewallRule -Group "Craft Conductor"`); Keep leaves it.

section: B. Firewall cleanup when a server is deleted
step: Two servers share a port, delete one - The rule stays (another server still uses the port).

section: B. Firewall cleanup when a server is deleted
step: Turn off the friends download - The "Craft Conductor: friends downloads (TCP 8766)" rule is offered for removal the same way.

section: B. Firewall cleanup when a server is deleted
step: Check my setup - Lists Craft Conductor rules for ports nothing uses any more, with a Remove button.

section: B. Firewall cleanup when a server is deleted
step: Remove the Java Craft Conductor installed - Windows' own `java` allow rules for that program path are offered for removal.

section: B. Firewall cleanup when a server is deleted
step: Uninstall or delete all Craft Conductor data - Offers to remove every rule in the group "Craft Conductor".

section: B. Firewall cleanup when a server is deleted
step: Answer No to Windows' prompt - A clear message; nothing half-removed; the server is still deleted.
Pick a pack whose loader differs from the form's loader - The browser shows all loaders, or says which loader it is filtering by, and the source (Modrinth/CurseForge) stays put (finding 37).
Pack with a false "Minecraft range" alarm - A pack that works is not blocked by the setup check (findings 33, 34, 35, 36).
CurseForge pack with a server pack over 512 MiB - Client-only mods do not end up on the server, or the user is told which to remove (findings 39, 44, 45).
Pack with mods that need manual download - Create is blocked until they are loaded or removed; removed mods do not come back as dependencies (finding 44).
Setup fails after a world was imported - A retry works; the imported world is not left behind (finding 43).
Forge server on Minecraft 26.x - The shim jar is kept and the server starts (finding 42).
World from a newer Minecraft than the server - A warning before import (finding 41).
Modded world on a server without those mods - Lists the missing mod data packs and game rules (finding 47).

A modpack server and a client on the real pack - The client can join; the panel says which mods differ from the pack (finding 48). Check in Prism: the server's mod files against the instance's `mods` folder.
Stop the failing setup - The failure message is plain words, not a Java stack trace (finding 40).
New server: playit.gg is chosen at first, its downsides are shown next to it, and the page says the whitelist will be on; Your Minecraft name puts you on the whitelist.

Windows, Friends page → playit.gg: nothing is downloaded before Download and install playit.gg is pressed; then the installer passes the checks (checksum and Developed Methods LLC's signature) and opens.

Open a port on my router: the risks are asked about first, then Craft Conductor picks a port from 30000 to 39999 (never 25565); Router (UPnP) and the Windows Firewall rule use it, and a friend on mobile data joins.
A server with Geyser and port forwarding: a UDP port is picked for Bedrock, written to Geyser's config and forwarded; a Bedrock player on mobile data joins.
A server reachable from the internet starts with the whitelist on; turning it off asks every time (Dashboard, Players, Settings, New server).

A server made by this version that becomes reachable later (Router on, a public address, a playit.gg address) gets its whitelist turned on, with a notice in the activity and the bell; one made before is left alone.
Invite links: Links work for offers 1, 3 or 7 days; after the last link ends, the friends' download port is closed and Router (UPnP) removes its mapping from the router within a minute.
Updating from 0.28.0 with a link set to 30 days or Until I make new ones: the release notes start with Before you update, and after the update the link has stopped, with a notice.
A player who joined through playit.gg: Ban IP is refused (it would ban this computer's own address), with a reminder to ban the name instead.
With only playit.gg's tray icon running (its agent stopped), the Dashboard doesn't say playit.gg is running.

section: Fix: Phone app notifications on Android (#117)
step: On an Android phone in the installed app, open Craft Conductor settings → Connections → Phone app: under This device, the sentence about notifications reads as one paragraph above the Turn on notifications here button (not squeezed beside it); after turning them on, ✓ Notifications are on for this device sits above Send a test and Turn off.

section: Fix: A CurseForge pack's mods for players stay at the pack's files (#95)
step: Make a server from a CurseForge modpack with an official server pack (All the Mods 11, say): on the Friends page, the pack's players-only mods show held at the pack's builds, and a friend who sets up through the invite gets those exact files (compare with the pack's own instance in Prism) and can join.

section: Fix: A Java that was slow to answer once isn't treated as missing
step: On Windows with an antivirus scanning, point [java.versions] at a freshly unzipped Java (or one on a slow USB drive) and start the server: if the first check times out, starting again a minute later finds that Java instead of saying it isn't Java or downloading another.

section: Fix: Mods only players need stay off the server (#93)
step: On a NeoForge server, add Iris Search from CurseForge (it needs Iris, which needs Sodium): Manage Mods lists Iris and Sodium as not installed because only players need them, the server starts, and a friend's download has Iris Search, Iris and Sodium.

section: Feature: Modrinth decides for CurseForge mods (#94)
step: New server → a CurseForge modpack with no server pack (or add Sodium from CurseForge to a server): the mods Modrinth says only run on players' computers go in the friends' download (their rows say so), and the server starts.

section: Feature: Move a mod to players' mods (#94)
step: Add a client-only mod that Modrinth doesn't know to a server so it stops at start: the Dashboard says it only runs on players' computers and offers Move … to players' mods; pressing it and starting again works, the mod is in the friends' download, and Manage Mods → Put back on the server undoes it.

Make a server from an older version of a modpack (Modrinth and CurseForge), change one of its config files and remove one pack mod, then Updates → Look for a new version of the pack → See what changes → Update the pack: the mods move to the new version's files, your config change and the removed mod stay, a friend on the real pack's new version can join, and a version that fails puts everything back.

section: Fix: The server runs the pack's loader build (#95)
step: Make a server from All the Mods 11 (CurseForge, NeoForge) and from a Modrinth NeoForge or Fabric pack: the Dashboard shows the pack's loader build (26.1.2.109 for All the Mods 11, not the newest), Updates -> Modpack says it's held, and a Prism client on the real pack joins without 'Incompatible client'. Updating the pack to a version with another loader build moves the server to it.

section: Feature: Hand downloads found by themselves
step: New server → a CurseForge modpack (or a CurseForge mod) with a file its author keeps to CurseForge: press its Download from CurseForge ↗ link and download it in Chrome or Edge, then in Firefox. Without dropping anything, Craft Conductor finds it in Downloads, says Found … in your Downloads folder, the orange Manage Mods glow and the warnings go, Create my server works, and the file is still in Downloads.

section: Feature: Hand downloads found by themselves
step: Save the hand-downloaded file in another folder (not Downloads): after pressing its link and coming back, the section asks Not found in your Downloads folder. Where did you save it?; Choose the folder… opens the folder browser in Downloads; open the other folder and press Just this time: it's found. Again with Always look here: Craft Conductor settings → Folders lists the folder, it's looked in for the next server too, and Forget takes it away.

section: Feature: Hand downloads found by themselves
step: Put another version of the mod in Downloads under the exact file name CurseForge lists: the row says wrong file and a message says it isn't the file CurseForge lists; nothing is loaded. Download the right one (it becomes name (1).jar): it's found and loaded.

section: Feature: Hand downloads found by themselves
step: Open the setup page from a phone or another computer (signed in as the owner): the section says what you download there is saved on that device; dropping the file on the section works. Signed in as an invited person with Manage mods on a server waiting for a hand download: the panel has the drop box but no Downloads line or Choose the folder….

section: Feature: Hand downloads found by themselves
step: Where Downloads is: on Windows, move Downloads to another drive (Downloads → Properties → Location) and check Craft Conductor finds the hand-downloaded file there; on a Mac, ~/Downloads; on Linux with a desktop whose Downloads folder has another name (another language, or XDG_DOWNLOAD_DIR changed). section: Feature: Choose where files are kept

Change… for Exports, open another drive, New folder…, Use this folder, then Use these folders: Saved., a README.txt in each chosen folder, the guided setup is offered afterwards, and the page isn't shown again (also after a reload).

section: Feature: Choose where files are kept

section: Feature: Choose where files are kept

section: Fix: Check my setup reads Windows Firewall with accented letters (#150)
step: On Windows, with a firewall rule for a program in a folder with accented letters (for example a server in C:\cc\servers\ünïcødé that Windows asked about, or any rule on Windows in another language): open Check my setup on a server whose port is allowed, then one whose port isn't. The Windows Firewall line says whether the port gets through (with Let them through Windows Firewall when it doesn't), not only that Windows asks the first time; nothing about 'charmap' or UnicodeDecodeError appears in Craft Conductor's window.
